title: What is man? (Psalm 8)
hookLine: the moon and stars, and yet God is mindful of us
carry: what are we, that you care?

cards: Go outside on a clear night, away from the streetlights, and look up long enough for your eyes to adjust. First a few stars. Then dozens.
Then a haze too many to count, and maybe the pale smear of the Milky Way. Out there it's easy to feel two things at once: very small, and strangely more awake than all week.
Long ago, someone stood under that same sky, with no telescopes and no streetlights, and the psalm's heading names him David. He wrote down a question people are still asking.

teach.b: Psalm eight opens and closes with the same line, in the King James Bible: "O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!" Praise as bookends.

teach.h: WHAT IS MAN, THAT THOU ART MINDFUL?
teach.b: In between, the question: "When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him?"
Notice the work of thy fingers. Not God's arm, not his mighty hand. Fingers, like someone doing fine embroidery.
The whole night sky is fingerwork. Next to that, what are we? A breath.

A speck. And yet God is mindful of us, remembers us, comes to see us. Then the psalm turns the other way: "For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour."

The Hebrew word there is elohim, which can mean God or heavenly beings. The King James says angels, and so does the letter to the Hebrews when it quotes this verse; some translations say a little lower than God.
And given dominion, the psalm says, over the sheep and oxen, the birds and the fish.

teach.h: O LORD OUR LORD, HOW EXCELLENT IS THY NAME.
teach.b: Some readers hear in that a charge to care for the world, not only to rule it. Hebrews hears these verses fulfilled in Jesus, crowned with glory after being made low.

how: Christians pray Psalm 8 in daily prayer and at services that give thanks for creation, and the letter to the Hebrews (chapter 2) reads it as pointing to Jesus.

o: a Hebrew word for a king who rules over the earth
a Hebrew word for the stars God set in the sky
a Hebrew word for a human being: small, yet remembered

games.q: what's inside Psalm 8 — tap the pairs.
p: a little lower than the angels

s: Psalm 8 begins and ends with the same line
"O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!"
it says elohim, which can mean God or heavenly beings. the King James and Hebrews 2 say angels.
the psalm calls the moon and stars the work of God's fingers
"thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars."

games.q: you're lying under the night sky, the moon and stars all around. the psalmist asks, what is man? what's the psalm's answer?
o: small, and yet remembered and crowned.
games.why: both at once: so small God need not notice, and yet God is mindful of us, and crowns us with glory and honor.

practice: Look up, through a window or outside; if it's daytime, the stars are still there behind the blue.
Let yourself feel small, one person on one planet circling one star among more than anyone can count, and then let the second half of the psalm in: and yet, remembered, cared for.
If you pray, ask the psalm's question out loud: what am I, that you care?

wordCard.voice: Enosh. One of the Hebrew words for a human being, the psalmist's word for how small we are under the stars, and yet remembered.

orig.note: Hebrew: what is man? Enosh is one of the Hebrew words for a human being.
